article_notes: 45 dogs clinically suspected of babesiosis in northern Portugal (2007-2009), all PCR positive (44 B. canis canis, 1 B. canis vogeli); co-infections in 9. The only severity-related result is mortality by co-infection status, given descriptively (no test). HCT and age were compared between co-infected and singly infected dogs, but co-infection is not a severity measure, so those comparisons were not extracted. Setting not stated (dogs from the region examined clinically); samples taken at presentation, treatment timing not stated.

severity_definitions.label: died or euthanised vs recovered
severity_definitions.definition: Dogs that died despite imidocarb treatment (n = 2, both co-infected) or were euthanised at the owners' request (n = 2) versus dogs that clinically recovered after imidocarb (n = 41). Follow-up horizon not stated.
severity_definitions.quote: Of the 45 dogs diagnosed with babesiosis, four (9%) died.

associations.marker_as_reported: co-infection with L. infantum, E. canis or H. canis (PCR and sequencing)
associations.species: B. canis canis (44/45), B. canis vogeli (1/45)
associations.statistic: mortality 2/9 (22%) in co-infected dogs vs 2/36 (6%, both euthanised) in dogs with B. canis canis only; no test
associations.quote: Despite treatment with imidocarb dipropionate, two dogs died (22%) out of the nine found co-infected (Table 3).
associations.location: Results, last paragraph; Table 3 (clinical outcome column)
associations.note: Mortality is given per exposure group (co-infected vs single infection), not co-infection per outcome group, so severe_value and comparison_value are left null (2/4 co-infected among dead dogs is not printed). The 2/36 (6%) figure for single infections is from the Discussion: 'From the 36 dogs found infected only with B. canis canis, two (6%) were euthanized'. The authors state co-infected dogs 'had a lower survival rate' but did no test. The two deaths in co-infected dogs were spontaneous; the two in single infections were owner-requested euthanasia.
